name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 executable MCP gateway built with the Machai AI framework. It discovers Machai FunctionTools and prompts supplied by separately packaged runtime libraries, converts tool parameter descriptors to MCP JSON Schema definitions, and exposes the resulting capabilities to MCP clients. The server deliberately does not bundle domain tools: deployments add their own automation, coding, data, or internal-platform capabilities through compatible tool JARs and service-provider registration. The org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer CLI selects synchronous STDIO by default, stateless HTTP when a port is supplied, or streamable HTTP when the session option is combined with a port. HTTP transports are hosted by Jetty. The stateless HTTP adapter publishes tools, prompts, and resources; the STDIO and streamable HTTP adapters publish tools and prompts. Configuration supports server metadata, an optional project directory, a properties file, and optional enabled-tool filtering, making the artifact suitable for desktop MCP clients, inspectors, remote agents, and reusable AI tool gateways.

usageContext: Publish separately packaged Machai FunctionTools and prompts to MCP clients

constructors.description: Creates a synchronous single-session MCP server that communicates on the hosting process standard input and output. Tools and prompts are loaded before startup.

examples.description: Creates a STDIO transport server with an explicit workspace context. Normal application deployments use the org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer CLI, which also performs tool discovery.

constructors.description: Creates a stateless synchronous HTTP MCP server. This transport can publish discovered tools, prompts, and resources through its Jetty servlet.

examples.description: Creates a stateless HTTP server, configures its listening port, and supplies a workspace for tools.

constructors.description: Creates a streamable synchronous HTTP MCP server that publishes discovered tools and prompts and can supply session information to prompt calls.

examples.description: Creates the session-aware HTTP server. For a complete deployment, invoke the CLI with both --port and --session.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Starts the MCP gateway and selects transport from CLI arguments. Without --port it starts STDIO; --port starts stateless HTTP; --port with --session starts streamable HTTP. It also accepts project directory, configuration file, advertised name, and advertised version options.

examples.snippet: java -cp machai-mcp-server.jar;team-tools.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer --projectDir C:/work/app --config C:/config/mcp.properties --name team-mcp --version 1.0.0 --port 45000 --session
examples.description: Install Java 17, build with mvn -Ppack install or obtain a release JAR, then place the server and a Machai-compatible tool JAR on the Windows classpath. Configure credentials required by the tool JAR and run this command to host a streamable HTTP MCP endpoint. Use : rather than ; as the classpath separator on Unix-like systems.

features.name: getConfigurator
features.description: Creates the properties configurator used during server initialization. If configFile is null, a missing default mcp.properties file is tolerated; an explicitly requested unreadable file causes java.io.IOException.

examples.description: Loads a chosen properties file in a custom Java integration. CLI deployments obtain the same configuration behavior with --config C:/config/mcp.properties.

features.name: toHumanReadable
features.description: Converts a discovered tool name to the lower-case kebab-case name exposed to MCP clients. For example, createReleaseNotes becomes create-release-notes; null and empty inputs produce an empty string.

examples.description: Returns create-release-notes. The server automatically applies this conversion while adapting discovered tools.

features.name: setPort
features.description: Sets the port used by either HTTP transport before server startup. The HTTP server configures a Jetty connector and servlet transport provider on this port.

examples.description: Configures port 45000 for a programmatically created stateless MCP server. The CLI alternative is --port 45000.

customizations.name: Runtime FunctionTools and prompt libraries
customizations.description: Extend the gateway by packaging Machai-compatible FunctionTools and prompt implementations in separate JARs with required service-provider registration. Add those JARs to the runtime classpath and the selected server discovers, adapts, and exposes their capabilities through MCP.

examples.description: Publishes a team tool JAR through stateless HTTP MCP. Connect a client to http://localhost:45000/mcp after startup.

customizations.name: MCP transport, context, and tool filtering
customizations.description: Use -d or --projectDir for a tool workspace, -c or --config for properties, -n or --name and -v or --version for advertised metadata, -p or --port for HTTP, and -s or --session for streamable HTTP. The enabledTools configuration property optionally limits registered tools; its values may be separated by spaces, commas, semicolons, or other whitespace.

examples.description: Configures a stateless HTTP server with explicit workspace context and client-visible metadata. Set enabledTools in the selected properties file when only a subset of discovered tools should be registered.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Shared MCP server boundary that manages project-directory context, optional enabled-tool filtering, tool registration, and transport startup hooks.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer.ToolSpecificationBuilder
studs.description: Transport boundary for creating MCP-specific tool specifications from a generic MCP tool definition and an invocation handler.

examples.title: Install and run a local STDIO MCP server
steps: Install Java 17 or a compatible newer Java runtime.
Download the release JAR from SourceForge or build the artifact from source with mvn -Ppack install.
Obtain a Machai-compatible FunctionTools JAR that includes its service-provider registration.
Configure credentials, model settings, and environment variables required by the chosen tools.
Configure a desktop MCP client to launch java -cp machai-mcp-server.jar;functional-tool-container.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.
Start the client and verify that discovered tools and prompts are listed before invoking a tool.
examples.description: No --port option selects STDIO. This is the practical installation pattern for a local desktop MCP client that launches the Java process; use : rather than ; as the classpath separator on Unix-like systems.

examples.title: Install, configure, and use a streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
steps: Install Java 17 and obtain the server JAR plus at least one compatible FunctionTools JAR.
Create an optional mcp.properties file containing tool settings and, if needed, an enabledTools list.
Configure credentials and other environment settings required by the deployed tool JAR.
Configure MCP Inspector, mcp-remote, or another client to connect to http://localhost:45000/mcp.
Inspect registered tools and prompts, then invoke a capability through the connected MCP client.
examples.description: This scenario starts session-aware streamable HTTP and gives tools a known workspace. Omit --session to use the stateless HTTP transport, which can also expose resources.
